question.leadin: The 1569 Union of Lublin joined this region with Lithuania, and it underwent three partitions before 1800.
question.text: Name this country, which was invaded by the Nazis on September 1, 1939 to start World War II. The Soviets invaded this country two weeks later.
question.clue: The Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact agreed to split this country between Germany and the Soviet Union.

swap.leadin: The firing of Anna Walentynowicz triggered a strike that led to the creation of this group.
swap.text: Name this trade union that grew from the 21 MKS Demands developed at the Gdansk shipyards.
swap.clue: The first prime minister elected from this organization spoke of the "thick line" that would demarcate his policies compared to the past.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Eastern European leaders.
question.text: Elected president of Poland in 1990, this man is famous for organizing the famous Soviet trade union, Solidarity.
question.clue: His wife, Danuta, claimed his Nobel Peace Prize for him in 1983.

swap.leadin: It was partitioned several times in the late 18th century.
swap.text: Name this region whose king Jan Sobieski III dispersed the Ottomans during the Second Siege of Vienna, which became a modern-day country with its capital at Warsaw.
swap.clue: In the middle ages, this nation was ruled by the Piast Dynasty, whose kings included Boleslaw the Brave and Casimir the Great.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the November Uprising.
question.text: This city in modern-day Poland was annexed by Austria in the wake of the November Uprising, losing its "Free City" status that had been granted by the Congress of Vienna. This city was the capital of Poland before Warsaw.
question.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

swap.leadin: Winged hussars from this polity charged to victory at battles such as Klushino and Kluzyn.
swap.text: Identify this polity formed following the Union of Lublin which dissolved following a series of partitions.
swap.clue: Monarchs agreed to the Henrician Articles and made individual commitments called the pacta conventa on becoming rulers of this country.

question.text: The Deluge began with this Cossack rebellion, in which the Zaporozhian Host rebelled against Polish-Lithuanian rule in Ukraine under its namesake leader.
question.clue: This confict's victorious leader avenged the failure ten years prior of Jakub Ostrzanin, thanks to the help of the Tatar cavalry.

swap.leadin: While every Weimar government aimed to incorporate this city, this city did not become German territory until the day after Germany began World War II.
swap.text: Name this League of Nations-run "Free City" that was an important port on the Baltic Sea and was primarily German-populated at the time of its invasion.
swap.clue: Woodrow Wilson's insistence that a country have access to the sea resulted in the creation of this city's namesake "corridor," which made East Prussia an exclave.

question.leadin: William Wilkinson was brought in from England to manage one of the burgeoning iron works in the early 19th century in this region.
question.text: Identify this region that was secured by Prussia following a successful defense of Chotusitz (KHO-too-zits) in 1742 during the War of Austrian Succession, which ended with Maria Theresa losing it to Prussia.
question.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

swap.leadin: During the reign of Augustus III, only one of these bodies succeeded in passing any laws at all.
swap.text: Name these Polish legislative bodies. A "great" one of these bodies passed the Constitution of May 3rd, 1791.
swap.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

question.text: The Janissary Revolt of 1622 followed a disastrous defeat at Choczim against this country, a combined commonwealth of two modern-day states ruled by the Jagiellon dynasty, with which the Ottomans had fought the Moldavian Magnate Wars. They often fought over Tatar and Cossack raids.
question.clue: Ruled by a form of government created by the Nihili Novi act, its main political doctrine could be summed up as "The King reigns but does not govern"; that political system was called the Golden Liberty.

swap.text: 12 members of the Communist Party were imprisoned for 'seditious conspiracy' in 1926 during a 'general' one of these events. Arthur Scargill led miners in one of these events in the 1980s.
swap.clue: The headline "Crisis? What Crisis?" was used to criticize James Callaghan's handling of a wave of these events that became known as the "Winter of Discontent."

question.text: At Grunwald, the Lithuanian forces were led by this Grand Duke of Lithuania. The Ostrow Agreement between this man and his cousin Jogaila ended the Lithuanian Civil War.
question.clue: This junior partner in the Ostrow ("AW-stroof") Agreement sent his nephew Prince Korybut to rule the Hussites.

swap.text: Under the command of Edigu and Temur Qutlugh ("KUT-lug"), the Horde won a victory over this state at the Battle of the Vorskla River. This state was led by Grand Duke Vytautas, who was a successor to Jogaila ("yo-GAI-wa").
swap.answerHtml: Grand Duchy of Lithuania [accept Kingdom of Lithuania; reject “Poland-Lithuania” or “Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania” or “Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth”]
swap.clue: Algirdas's victory over the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters drove the greatest expansionary period of this polity, whose ruler Vytautus's involvement with the Samogitian uprisings and incessant warring with the Teutonic Knights helped prompt the Battle of Grunwald. For 15 points, identify this Grand Duchy which participated in the 1569 Union of Lublin.

question.leadin: Identify some things about a historical movement.
question.text: Round Table Agreement occurred under the rule of this man, the last communist ruler of Poland. He declared martial law when he came to power in order to ward off a possible Soviet invasion.
question.clue: In 2008, the IPN put this man on trial brutal crackdown which entrenched him as dictator in 1982.

swap.leadin: This ruler defeated the Yaroslav the Wise at the Battle of Bug River and his long war with Henry II was ended with the Peace of Bautzen.
swap.text: Name this member of the Piast Dynasty that established the Prince's Law and was succeeded by Mieszko II.
swap.answerHtml: Bolesław I Chrobry (prompt on “Bolesław”; accept Bolesław the Great; accept Bolesław the Valiant; accept Bolesław the Brave; accept Bolesław Chrobry)
swap.clue: This ruler redeemed the corpse of Saint Adalbert for a sack of gold, and was given a supposed copy of the Holy Lance known as St. Maurice's Spear at the Congress of Gniezno.

question.leadin: Spurred by threats from Russia in the Livonian War, this arrangement replaced the Union of Krewo, which established for only a personal union. FTPE.
question.text: Name this 1569 agreement which united Poland and Lithuania into a single federation.
question.clue: The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was formed when both countries agreed to the provisions of this document, named for a city in Poland.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Polish history.
swap.text: This poet, the author of Pan Tadeusz and The Books of the Polish Nation, died in Istanbul trying to raise a Polish battalion to fight the Russians in 1855 after years of championing Poland as the "Christ of nations."

question.leadin: Apocryphally, this dynasty came to power after the cruel Prince Popiel II ("POPE-yell the second") was imprisoned and eaten alive by rats and mice.
question.text: Name this dynasty that succeeded the Popielid dynasty. A history by Gallus Anonymus claims that this dynasty was founded by a namesake wheelwright with an always-full cellar, an ancestor of Boleslaw ("bo-LESS-waff") the Brave.
question.clue: Earlier, when this dynasty's ruler Henry II the Pious was killed at the Battle of Legnica, its Silesian branch was left exposed.

swap.text: This Polish ethnic group targeted by the Germanization program was later one of the few labeled as capable of Germanization by the Nazis, an effort they did little to comply with; nonetheless, many members of this ethnic group centered in Pomerania were expelled along with the Germans after the war.
